Crypto Break-Even Calculator

Every position starts underwater — this is the price where fees and funding are paid off and real profit begins.

How it is calculated

break-even move = 2 × taker fee + funding rate × (hours / 8)   |   BE price = entry × (1 ± move)

Fees are charged on the whole position, so at high leverage they eat a startling share of your margin: a 0.11% round trip is 2.2% of margin at 20x and 11% at 100x — before the price has moved anywhere. Funding compounds the drag on positions held across 8-hour marks, which is why overnight scalps at max leverage quietly bleed.

Worked example

Long at $60,000, 20x, 0.055% taker each way, +0.01%/8h funding, held 24h: fees 0.110% + funding 0.030% = 0.140%. Break-even price $60,084 — and that 0.14% costs 2.8% of your margin at 20x.

FAQ

Do limit orders change the break-even?

Yes — maker fees are far lower (often 0.02% or even rebates) than taker fees. Entering and exiting with limit orders can cut the fee half of your break-even by two thirds or more, which matters enormously for high-frequency or high-leverage styles.

Can funding be in my favor?

Yes. Funding flows between longs and shorts depending on the rate sign: positive rates mean longs pay shorts, negative rates mean shorts pay longs. Holding against the crowded side actually earns funding — enter a negative rate in the calculator to see it reduce your break-even.

Why does my ticket show a loss right after entry?

The entry fee is deducted immediately and the mark price usually sits a spread away from your fill. That small instant drawdown is exactly the cost this calculator prices in — the position needs the break-even move before it is genuinely green.
